The primary advantage of FIFO is its simplicity and fairness, as every job receives equal treatment based on arrival time rather than priority or speed. This makes it ideal for systems where job sizes are similar and the goal is to minimize waiting times for all users.

Head-of-line blocking occurs when a job is processed before others waiting in the queue, causing the queue to grow and potentially blocking subsequent requests. This can lead to system instability if the queue becomes too long, though it is generally acceptable for short-lived tasks.
